payload.text: Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, in which the dopant suppresses negative-electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism. The finalized independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Operation must be suspended below 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
